attempts.rationale: Testing a simple mean over the full pool to gauge baseline performance under trend-dominated, high predictability regime.
test a weighted combination using inverse_error to see if error‐based weighting improves over mean in a trend‑dominated, high predictability series.
The series has trend-dominated regime with unstable ranking; a robust non-weighted combination like median may perform better than mean.
test a per-horizon weighted combo using the top‑k pool to see if horizon‑specific gains help under the trend‑dominated, high predictability regime.
The series is trend-dominated with moderate seasonality and unstable ranking; a robust trimmed mean might reduce influence of outlier models.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings, so a robust method like DBA over the full pool may capture shared trends better than simple weighted averages.

The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings; a robust per-horizon weighting may capture shifting best models.
Try a robust per-horizon weighted combination on the stable pool4 using inverse_error weights to capture complementary strengths while keeping subset small.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable rankings; a robust combination like a median over a smaller, more stable pool (pool4) may outperform the full‑pool mean.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable rankings; a robust DBA on a smaller, more stable pool may capture complementary strengths better than full‑pool DBA.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a trimmed‑mean over a reduced, stable pool may provide robustness.

decision.justification: Selected 'dba' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9746. Series context: trend strength 0.8121 and seasonal strength 0.3768; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.119); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.521.
